We spent $2M telling the world to stop hiring humans.\
\
Today we’re taking it back.\
\
And in even more shocking news: Artisan is hiring a human BDR.\
\
The billboards were never a lie. Ava the AI BDR does outreach better than most humans. But she can’t legally cold call. She can’t shake a hand at a conference. She can’t be human.\
\
So we built the tools for the humans. A dialer and a full rep toolkit, inside Artisan. Your reps do the human work. Ava does EVERYTHING else. Leads, signals, personalization, objections, meetings booked, all autonomous.\
\
That’s already how the biggest teams on Artisan run. One of them has Ava working alongside 1,000+ human reps.\
\
Now we’re proving the super-BDR thesis on ourselves. The one BDR we hire will outperform most companies’ entire team. \
\
Stop hiring humans led to billions of impressions and millions in ARR. But it’s time for the next era.\
\
Next Monday: our manifesto and new slogan. The future is humans AND AI, not humans or AI.

From 0 → $7M ARR in 18 months. $35M+ raised.\

That’s @getartisan — the SF startup building human-like AI employees to replace your bloated GTM stack… and maybe kick off the next Industrial Revolution.\
\
In this episode of TALKS WITH DASHA, I sat down with @jasparcj to talk about what it takes to build a successful company.

Artisan, the AI sales agent startup founded by Jaspar Carmichael-Jack, recently raised $25 million in Series A funding, led by Glade Brook Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, Day One Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, and others. Founded in 2024, Artisan initially garnered attention with its bold “Stop Hiring Humans” campaign, positioning itself in the rapidly growing AI sales development representative (SDR) market. Despite early-stage challenges, including customer churn and issues with AI performance, the company has made significant strides, refining its AI agent, Ava, and achieving $5 million in annual recurring revenue with 250 customers. Artisan is also working on new AI products, such as Aaron for inbound messaging and Aria, a meeting manager assistant, both set to launch by the end of 2025. Carmichael-Jack, who co-founded the company with Sam Stallings, continues to steer Artisan as CEO, emphasizing the importance of human labor in AI-driven environments.\

You create value by doing three things:\

- Identify problems\
- Create solutions\

\
What problems can you solve for the people around you?\
\
Figure them out, solve them, scale that solution.\

Roughly $300 an hour.\

If you're reading this, you've probably already realized that I made a huge mistake.\

From $300 an hour to $600 an hour.\

\
I could now work half as much and make the same, or I could work exactly the same amount and make double.\

There's a really big lesson in here:\

You can give yourself a raise in free time, but you have to let yourself keep it.\

That time can be invested back into you and your business.\

Can you upgrade chilli con carne? YES! Make it brothy! 🌶️🍲 Recipe below ⬇️ \
\
For the chilli mince:\
2 tbsp olive oil\
500g 5% fat beef mince\
 1 x 400g tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed\
 1 tsp ground cumin\
 1 tsp smoked paprika\
 2 tsp garlic powder\
 2 tsp ground coriander\
 1 tsp dried oregano\
 1 tsp hot chilli powder\
\
For the broth:\
6 garlic cloves, finely minced\
 1 tbsp tomato purée\
 2 tbsp Tesco Finest Chipotle Marinade Paste\
 2 tsp ground cumin\
 2 tsp smoked paprika\
 1 tsp cinnamon\
 ½ beef stock cube, made up to 850ml\
 Juice of 1 lime\
 15g fresh coriander, finely chopped\
200g easy cook long grain & wild rice\
Fresh coriander, red pickled onions and sliced avocado, to serve (optional)\
\
1. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the beef mince, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Fry for 5-10 minutes until brown and starting to caramelise. \
2. Add the kidney beans, spices and a splash of water. Stir well and cook for another 5 minutes, or until the water has evaporated. Transfer to a bowl and keep warm.\
3. For the broth, in the same pan, combine the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, tomato purée, chipotle paste and broth spices. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.\
4. Pour in the stock and stir well. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the pack instructions. \
5. Stir the lime juice and chopped coriander into the broth. Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chilli mince. Pour over the broth and finish with fresh coriander, red pickled onions and sliced avocado, if you wish.

Swalty cracker bark with Jacob's cream crackers. Recipe below ⬇️\
\
150g 75% dark chocolate, roughly chopped\
12 Jacob’s crackers\
5 tbsp salted caramel sauce\
40g pecan halves, finely chopped (optional)\
60g all-butter fudge, finely chopped\
Pinch sea salt flakes\
\
1. Line a large (roughly 35cm x 25cm) shallow baking tray with baking paper.\
2. Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of gently simmering water, ensuring the base of the bowl doesn’t touch the water. Alternatively, melt in short bursts in the microwave. Set aside.\
3. Arrange the Jacob’s crackers in a single layer on the baking tray.  Spoon over 4 tbsp caramel and smooth into an even layer using the back of a dessert spoon. Chill in the freezer for 10 mins or in the fridge for 30 mins until firm.\
4. Pour over the chocolate and smooth to cover the caramel. Drizzle over the remaining caramel, then sprinkle with the pecans, if using, the fudge and a pinch of sea salt. \
5. Chill in the fridge for 1 hr, or the freezer for 20 mins, until fully set then cut into roughly 16 different shaped pieces.\
6. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week or freeze for up to 3 months.

30 minute salmon parcels anyone? Recipe below ⬇️ \
\
 50g Tesco Finest cavolo nero kale, stems removed and roughly chopped\
1 rosemary sprig, needles picked\
2 thyme sprigs, leaves picked\
2 dill sprigs \
1 small garlic clove, crushed\
1 lemon, juice of ½ and ½ cut into slices\
10g Parmesan, grated\
½ tsp Dijon mustard\
25g 50% less fat crème fraîche\
1 leek, finely sliced\
400g tin butter beans, drained and rinsed\
2 Tesco Finest Scottish Salmon Fillets\
2 tbsp olive oil \
\
1. Preheat the oven to gas 7, 220°C, fan 200°C. Cut 2 large squares of baking paper, big enough to wrap around and seal the fish.\
2. Put the cavolo nero in a large bowl and cover with boiling water. Place a plate on top and leave to steep for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water to cool, then use your hands to squeeze out the remaining water.\
3. Put the cavolo nero in a blender with the rosemary, thyme, dill, garlic, lemon juice, Parmesan, mustard, crème fraîche and 2 tbsp water, then blend until smooth. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.\
4. Divide the beans and leeks between the centre of each sheet of baking paper. Put the salmon fillets skin-side down on top and season with salt and pepper. Spread the sauce over each fillet then top with the lemon slices. \
5. Lift the sides of the baking paper up to join over the salmon, then scrunch the paper tightly together to seal the parcels. Put the parcels on a baking tray and bake for 15 minutes or until the salmon flakes easily. Leave to rest for 3 minutes before carefully opening the parcels.

Understanding your anatomy can help you recognize changes and explain what you’re experiencing. But too many women have never been taught what to look for, what questions to ask, or that help is available.\

Feeling overwhelmed in the supplement aisle is a predictable result of an industry that sells you a dozen bottles before anyone has looked at what you’re actually missing. If you’re in perimenopause and don’t know where to start, start with the gaps.\
\
In my practice, I begin with fiber and vitamin D. About 95 percent of American adults don’t get enough fiber, according to a 2017 review in the American Journal of Lifestyle Medicine. That shortfall matters more in the zone of chaos, when falling estrogen is already pushing LDL cholesterol and blood sugar in the wrong direction. Log your food in a nutrition tracker app for a week before you buy anything; it’ll show you exactly how many grams of fiber you’re getting. I’ve seen patients land well under 25 grams a day without realizing it.\
\
Vitamin D is different: no app can tell you where you stand. Ask your clinician for a 25-hydroxy vitamin D level, because you can’t know your dose until you know your number.\
\
Track your protein in that same app, because in my clinic it’s the other gap I see constantly. Muscle is your metabolic and skeletal insurance in midlife, and you can’t build it without enough protein. Creatine is one of the most studied supplements for muscle, and the research in midlife women looks strongest when it’s paired with strength training.\
\
Fill the gaps with real food first. When nutrition can’t get you there, that’s when a supplement earns its place. (Full disclosure: these are from my company, The Pause Life: Fiber GDX, our vitamin D3, K2, and omega-3 combo, and Protein + Creatine. All are NSF certified and third-party tested, because in an industry with almost no federal oversight before a product hits the shelf, you should know what’s in the bottle.) If you take a blood thinner, talk to your clinician before starting vitamin K or fish oil, and if you have kidney disease, check with them before adding creatine.\
\
You deserve a strategy, not a shopping cart.\
\
This content is educational and is not medical advice.\
Source: Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. American Journal of Lifestyle Medicine, 2017.

For my mother. For my grandmother. For my daughters. 🤍\
\
As I grieve the loss of my mother, I’m holding close the love that connects the generations of women in my family.\
\
I cannot control everything about how I age. But I can take steps today to protect my strength, support my brain health, and lower my risk of frailty and dementia.\
\
That is part of my “why.” Why I lift weights. Why I move my body. Why I pay attention to nutrition, sleep, and the supplements I choose based on my individual needs.\
\
There are no guarantees. But I have access to knowledge and resources my mother and grandmother never had. I want to use them, for myself and for my daughters.\
\
It is about taking what we know now and carrying it forward.\
\
I want my daughters to see that growing older is worth preparing for. That their health deserves attention long before something goes wrong. And that caring for themselves belongs on the list, too.\
\
I carry my mother and grandmother with me. And I hope the choices I make today become part of the legacy I leave my girls.\
\

There is a profound vulnerability in being a patient.\
 \
When something feels wrong, when you're scared, when you no longer recognize yourself or understand what's happening in your own body, you're placing enormous trust in another human being.\
 \
As a physician, I never want to lose sight of what that means.\
 \
Patients come to us with more than symptoms. They come with fears, questions, uncertainty, and the hope that someone will help them make sense of what they're experiencing. The doctor-patient relationship is built on trust, not just medical expertise. And that trust is shaped by how we listen, how we respond, and how we care for people when the answers aren't immediately clear.\
 \
We won't always have the answers. But we can always make room for the questions. We can acknowledge uncertainty without dismissing someone's experience. We can remember that what may be a routine appointment for us can be one of the most frightening moments in someone else's life.\
 \
Being listened to isn't a courtesy. It's part of being cared for. And every patient deserves that.\
\

The real ones know how much time it actually takes to track down the right assets BEFORE any editing takes place.\
\
Because of this, my team and I were able to produce AND launch 55 ads in JUST ONE DAY.\
\
Here’s the whole process we went through:\
\
1. Started with a pile of raw assets: hundreds of iPhone photos of sample product plus a few e-comm shots, all dumped into a shared @dropbox folder. No plan yet.\
\
2. Used ChatGPT for competitor research: specifically which competitor ads were pulling the highest impressions, plus mining their negative customer reviews so my product could fill that gap.\
\
3. Had ChatGPT reference the photos in the Dropbox folder and recommend which images best suited the ad angles we were about to make.\
\
4. Turned those angles into a creative matrix across the five formats and personas we wanted to target.\
\
5. Built a quick shot list from that matrix so I could film fast.\
\
6. Reviewed the recommendations, made a few edits, and saved the plan back to Dropbox  so the team could access it alongside the source images.\
\
7. Divided the work across the team and started producing the statics. Ads out within a few hours.\
\
Ngl, it’s really one of those “thank god for ai” use cases for me :)\

The most ethical thing you can do as a business owner or manager this month?\
\
Redraw your org chart.\
\
Let me explain.\
\
Whether you like it or not, AI agents are joining our teams.\
\
They have tasks. They have deliverables.\
\
They already influence the work your team is shipping. \
\
And with advancements like what @atlassian just announced at Team ’26 Europe in Amsterdam, their new Agentic Multiplayer Protocol, or AMP, we’re getting much closer to a world where AI agents are not just tools.\
\
They are visible, governed, accountable teammates.\
\
Which means the question is no longer:\
\
“Should we use AI?”\
\
The question is:\
\
How do we manage humans and AI agents as one team?\
\
Who owns the agent? What can it access? Who can see its work?\
\
When does a human step in? Who is ultimately accountable for the deliverable?\
\
This is what your new org chart should answer.\
\
Because your team probably uses a lot of AI already. \
\
But if you don’t know who that work is owned by or making approvals…\
\
Then you have a fake org chart.\
